body:
## For the Owner

**What This Does:** Chete gets a Settings window. You choose how long to keep clips, whether to keep copies from your iPhone, iPad or other Macs, and whether Chete opens at login. You can also delete all your clips, export them to a file, and bring them back. Chete asks before it deletes or replaces anything.

**Why:** These are the choices Chete's plan promises, in one place.

**What Changed Since Your Review:** Every line of text is shorter and plainer, as you asked. The rows and switches are the same. The theme switch you want is kept as #121, for when Lexicon is ready.

**Does It Change Your Apps?** Not yet. You'll see this window when you try the finished Chete. The first time you turn on Open at login, macOS tells you Chete was added to your Login Items.

**What to Do:** Read the two pictures below. If they read well, approve. If not, choose Request changes and say what to change.

Light:

![Chete's settings, light](https://github.com/amansinghphotos/Sagar/blob/20b51b5/Tests/CheteKitTests/Pictures/settings-light.png?raw=true)

Dark:

![Chete's settings, dark](https://github.com/amansinghphotos/Sagar/blob/20b51b5/Tests/CheteKitTests/Pictures/settings-dark.png?raw=true)

<details><summary>Checklist for the Agents</summary>

For #61

- [x] This closes exactly one issue, named above.
- [x] The test was written first and failed before the code, or this changes no code.
- [x] `Scripts/check` is green on my machine.
- [x] The reviewer agent read the newest commit and this description. Its reply is a comment here that names that commit, and each finding is fixed or answered there.
- [x] Nothing outside the slice was touched.

Built only from Look: `GroupBlock`, `SettingRow`, `Segmented`, `Switch` and `Pill`, with type roles, `Role` and `Space`; no colour, font or size named in the Kit. Apple's own confirmation dialog, save panel and open panel appear only when he clicks. Open at login uses `SMAppService.mainApp`, which needs no entitlement; the spec already names the Login Items request.

`Choices` keeps settings the moment they change and trims older clips at once when the time is shortened; it deletes every clip, exports the history as the plain file `History` already writes (now also as data, for the save panel), and brings one back. Tests use temporary folders and a test key: shortening deletes what is older, the switch is kept, deleting all keeps the settings, and an export brought back on another folder is the same.

Look, for screen readers, as the tour's accessibility audit asked: a sliding choice's options are buttons that can be pressed and say which is chosen; a switch acts as a switch, named by the screen; icons beside a setting's words are hidden, since the words say it. Gallery pictures are unchanged. The settings window is named, as Chete's window is, and is not brought back when Chete opens, so it opens only when asked.

Merging: #97 is merged, and main is merged into this branch. With #100, which is open: `CheteScene` gains one line, the settings window, at the top of its body, apart from #97's and #100's changes, and the new tour step sits at the top of the tour, apart from #100's at the bottom. Whichever of these lands last adds two small things, noted on #61: a Settings… item in #100's menu-bar menu, since an app with no Dock icon has no menu of its own, and telling #97's list to reload after Delete All or Bring Back.

Words: the owner asked, here and on #108, for plain, warm text, now the rule in SPEC.md section 8. Every line in Settings, its two questions and its error lines are rewritten; Chete's shared words (clips, Export, Bring Back, Open at login) are left in the chats' shared notes so #100 and #108 use the same ones.

Tour: audits the settings window, changes how long clips are kept to a month, quits, opens Chete again and finds a month still chosen. It passed on GitHub's Mac on 11fcee2.

Not done here: deleting clips as they pass the chosen age while Chete stays open, now #111. Shortening the time deletes older clips at once; the daily deletion belongs beside the watcher, which #97 changes, so it follows once #97 merges.

</details>
